newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end up as clampdown fears ease.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end up as clampdown fears ease.

text.p: China's share indices ended up across the board on Friday, led by solid rises in domestic A shares as investors shrugged off fears of possible official intervention to cool the markets down, brokers said.

But the official Xinhua news agency said after the market closed on Friday that China's State Council, or cabinet, had decided to raise the stamp tax on stock trading to 0.5 percent from the current 0.3 percent from May 10.

Brokers said the move would not in itself bring the markets down significantly, but it sends a signal that the government wants to cool down trading. They added that the markets were likely to fall slightly on Monday and then rebound.
The Shanghai B index ended Friday up 0.796 points, or 0.85 percent, at 94.131 on volume of 33.304 million shares worth $22.644 million, compared with $23.091 million on Thursday.
The Shanghai A index surged 66.254 points, or 4.51 percent, to 1,534.115 on turnover of 13.05 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index soared 188.088 points, or 4.60 percent, to 4,280.214.
Domestic institutions bought Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development following gains in the company's A shares, helping to push the B index up, brokers said.
Shanghai Lujiazui ended up $0.054, or 3.57 percent, at $1.564 on volume of 2.7 million shares.
"There was bargain-hunting triggered by the gains in Lujiazui and the rise in the A shares," one broker said. "But many investors are still sidelined due to concerns over a clampdown."
"The movement of the A share index will determine the direction of B shares in the near future," another broker said.
Shanghai Worldbest was the star on institutional buying, surging $0.063, or 9.44 percent, to $0.730 on volume of 1.4 million shares.
Market giant Shanghai Chlor Alkali Chemical was the most actively traded share on bargain-hunting late in the session, up $0.002, or 0.54 percent, to $0.366 on volume of 3.3 million shares.
The Shenzhen B share index gained 3.01 points, or 1.71 percent, to 179.62 on turnover of HK$167.55 million, against Thursday's HK$215.08 million.
"The solid A share gains boosted sentiment in the B share market," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The Shenzhen A share index gained 23.22 points, or 4.63 percent, to 525.14 on turnover of 17.4 billion yuan, compared with 20.2 billion yuan on Thursday.
On the B share market, refrigerator maker Hefei Meran Co Ltd, the most actively traded counter, was the star, up HK$0.68, or 7.44 percent, to HK$9.82 on volume of 3.5 million shares.
